primary_diagnosis: Secondary hypertension (primary aldosteronism / renal artery stenosis / other endocrine causes)
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with stage‑2 hypertension refractory to monotherapy, obesity, OSA, dyslipidemia, prediabetes, and a markedly elevated creatinine. The combination of uncontrolled BP, metabolic syndrome features, and renal dysfunction points to secondary hypertension as the most likely driver, with untreated OSA and metabolic syndrome acting as major amplifiers. Renal impairment appears hypertensive in origin but requires confirmation. Liver enzyme elevation, anemia with thrombocytosis, and platelet abnormalities suggest additional overlapping pathologies (alcoholic or non‑alcoholic liver disease, iron‑deficiency anemia, possible essential thrombocythemia). Cardiovascular risk is high, warranting evaluation for silent CAD and HFpEF. Thyroid dysfunction and vitamin D deficiency are lower‑priority but easily reversible contributors.

recommended_workup: Renin activity and plasma aldosterone concentration with aldosterone‑to‑renin ratio (screen for primary aldosteronism)
Renal artery duplex ultrasound or CT angiography (evaluate for renal‑artery stenosis)
Plasma metanephrines or 24‑hour urinary catecholamines (rule out pheochromocytoma)
Repeat serum creatinine and cystatin‑C; calculate eGFR using CKD‑EPI; obtain urine albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio
Comprehensive iron studies (serum iron, ferritin, TIBC) and reticulocyte count
Repeat complete blood count in 4–6 weeks; if thrombocytosis persists, order JAK2 V617F, CALR, MPL mutation panel
Polysomnography report review; initiate or titrate CPAP therapy if not already in use
Fasting lipid panel after ≥6 weeks of statin therapy; consider high‑intensity statin if LDL remains >70 mg/dL
Fasting glucose and/or 2‑hour oral glucose tolerance test
Liver panel (AST, ALT, GGT, ALP, bilirubin) plus hepatic ultrasound; order hepatitis B/C serologies and calculate AST/ALT ratio
Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test (AUDIT‑C) to quantify intake
BNP or NT‑proBNP and transthoracic echocardiogram (assess for HFpEF)
Coronary artery calcium scoring or stress imaging for subclinical CAD
Structured medication adherence interview and pharmacy refill review
Home or 24‑hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring
